# Langford sequences L(2,n) exist iff n ≡ 0 or 3 (mod 4)
n = 31

print(f"n mod 4 = {n % 4}")
print(f"Langford sequence L(2,{n}) exists: {n % 4 in [0, 3]}")

from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
from pysat.card import *

n = 31
length = 2 * n  # 62

# We'll use a SAT solver approach
# Variables: x[v][p] = True if value v is placed at position p
# v ranges from 1 to n, p ranges from 0 to length-1

# For each value v, if it's at position p, the other copy is at position p + v + 1
# So we need: x[v][p] <-> x[v][p+v+1]

# Let's encode this
solver = Glucose3()

# Create variable mapping: var(v, p) for v in 1..n, p in 0..length-1
def var(v, p):
    return (v - 1) * length + p + 1  # 1-indexed for SAT

num_vars = n * length

# Constraint 1: For each value v, if placed at position p, also at position p+v+1
# x[v][p] <-> x[v][p+v+1] for valid p
for v in range(1, n + 1):
    for p in range(length):
        p2 = p + v + 1
        if p2 < length:
            # x[v][p] <-> x[v][p2]
            # This means: x[v][p] -> x[v][p2] and x[v][p2] -> x[v][p]
            solver.add_clause([-var(v, p), var(v, p2)])
            solver.add_clause([-var(v, p2), var(v, p)])
        elif p2 == length:
            # p2 is out of bounds, so x[v][p] must be False
            solver.add_clause([-var(v, p)])

# Constraint 2: Each position has exactly one value
# For each position p, exactly one v has x[v][p] = True
for p in range(length):
    # At least one value at position p
    solver.add_clause([var(v, p) for v in range(1, n + 1)])
    # At most one value at position p (pairwise)
    for v1 in range(1, n + 1):
        for v2 in range(v1 + 1, n + 1):
            solver.add_clause([-var(v1, p), -var(v2, p)])

# Constraint 3: Each value v appears exactly twice (i.e., at exactly one pair of positions)
# Since x[v][p] <-> x[v][p+v+1], we just need to ensure v appears at least once
# Actually, we need to ensure v appears at some valid position pair
# For each v, at least one position p where p+v+1 < length
for v in range(1, n + 1):
    valid_positions = [p for p in range(length) if p + v + 1 < length]
    solver.add_clause([var(v, p) for p in valid_positions])

print(f"Number of variables: {num_vars}")
print(f"Solving...")

if solver.solve():
    model = solver.get_model()
    print("SAT!")
    
    # Extract solution
    seq = [0] * length
    for v in range(1, n + 1):
        for p in range(length):
            if var(v, p) in model:
                seq[p] = v
                seq[p + v + 1] = v
    
    print(f"Sequence: {seq}")
    print(f"Length: {len(seq)}")
    
    # Verify

        assert positions[1] - positions[0] == v + 1, f"Value {v} positions {positions}, gap {positions[1] - positions[0]}"
    
    print("Verification passed!")
else:
    print("UNSAT")

solver.delete()

from pysat.solvers import Glucose3

n = 31
length = 2 * n  # 62

# Better encoding:
# For each value v, we choose a starting position p (0-indexed) where the first copy goes.
# The second copy goes at position p + v + 1.
# So for value v, valid starting positions are 0, 1, ..., length - v - 2.

# Variables: start[v][p] = True if value v starts at position p
# v ranges from 1 to n, p ranges from 0 to length - v - 2

def var(v, p):
    # v in 1..n, p in 0..(length-v-2)
    return (v - 1) * length + p + 1

solver = Glucose3()

# Constraint 1: Each value v starts at exactly one position
for v in range(1, n + 1):
    max_p = length - v - 2  # last valid starting position
    positions = list(range(max_p + 1))
    
    # At least one
    solver.add_clause([var(v, p) for p in positions])
    
    # At most one (pairwise)
    for i in range(len(positions)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(positions)):
            solver.add_clause([-var(v, positions[i]), -var(v, positions[j])])

# Constraint 2: Each position is occupied by at most one value
# For each position pos, at most one (v, p) pair covers it
# Position pos is covered by value v if p == pos or p + v + 1 == pos
# i.e., p == pos or p == pos - v - 1

for pos in range(length):
    # Find all (v, p) pairs that cover position pos
    covering = []
    for v in range(1, n + 1):
        max_p = length - v - 2
        # v covers pos if starting at pos (first copy)
        if pos <= max_p:
            covering.append(var(v, pos))
        # v covers pos if starting at pos - v - 1 (second copy)
        p2 = pos - v - 1
        if 0 <= p2 <= max_p:
            covering.append(var(v, p2))
    
    # At most one of these can be true
    for i in range(len(covering)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(covering)):
            solver.add_clause([-covering[i], -covering[j]])

# Constraint 3: Each position is occupied by at least one value
for pos in range(length):
    covering = []
    for v in range(1, n + 1):
        max_p = length - v - 2
        if pos <= max_p:
            covering.append(var(v, pos))
        p2 = pos - v - 1
        if 0 <= p2 <= max_p:
            covering.append(var(v, p2))
    solver.add_clause(covering)

print(f"Solving...")

if solver.solve():
    model = solver.get_model()
    print("SAT!")
    
    # Extract solution
    seq = [0] * length
    for v in range(1, n + 1):
        max_p = length - v - 2
        for p in range(max_p + 1):
            if var(v, p) in model:
                seq[p] = v
                seq[p + v + 1] = v
                break
    
    print(f"Sequence: {seq}")
    print(f"Length: {len(seq)}")
    
    # Verify
    for v in range(1, n + 1):
        positions = [i for i, val in enumerate(seq) if val == v]
        assert len(positions) == 2, f"Value {v} appears {len(positions)} times"
        assert positions[1] - positions[0] == v + 1, f"Value {v} positions {positions}, gap {positions[1] - positions[0]}"
    
    # Check all positions filled
    assert all(x != 0 for x in seq), "Not all positions filled"
    
    print("Verification passed!")
else:
    print("UNSAT")

solver.delete()

seq = [31, 29, 30, 26, 24, 28, 21, 27, 18, 16, 25, 13, 11, 23, 6, 22, 5, 1, 20, 1, 19, 6, 5, 17, 11, 13, 16, 18, 21, 24, 26, 29, 31, 30, 28, 27, 25, 23, 22, 20, 19, 17, 15, 12, 14, 9, 10, 2, 3, 4, 2, 8, 3, 7, 4, 9, 12, 10, 15, 14, 8, 7]

# Full verification
n = 31
length = 62

assert len(seq) == length, f"Length is {len(seq)}, expected {length}"

for v in range(1, n + 1):
    positions = [i for i, val in enumerate(seq) if val == v]
    assert len(positions) == 2, f"Value {v} appears {len(positions)} times"
    gap = positions[1] - positions[0]
    assert gap == v + 1, f"Value {v} at positions {positions}, gap is {gap}, expected {v+1}"

# Check all values 1..31 appear
for v in range(1, n + 1):
    assert v in seq, f"Value {v} not in sequence"

print("All verifications passed!")
print(f"Sequence: {seq}")
